title: Synchronous and asynchronous Monte Carlo dynamics of mean-field spin glasses with rotationally invariant couplings: what they share and where they differ
abstract: We compare two Markov chain Monte Carlo dynamics for Ising spin glasses with rotationally invariant couplings: the synchronous Monte Carlo method (SyncMC), which updates all spins in parallel with the help of Gaussian auxiliary fields, and asynchronous Metropolis-Hastings dynamics, which updates one spin at a time. Using the Guionnet-Maïda formula, we derive the dynamical mean-field theory of both dynamics in terms of the R-transform of the coupling spectrum. The two effective single-spin processes share a retarded self-interaction and a Gaussian noise; SyncMC has, in addition, an instantaneous self-coupling and a noise that depends only on the response function. These additional terms act only on the fastest time scale, so that the equations for slow time scales, including the fluctuation-dissipation ratio and, for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, the Parisi equation, are the same for the two dynamics. Simulations of the random orthogonal and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models confirm that both dynamics approach the same fluctuation-dissipation relations, differing only in how many updates they need to do so.
summary: This paper theoretically compares synchronous and asynchronous Monte Carlo dynamics for mean-field spin glasses. Using Dynamical Mean-Field Theory, the authors show that although the microscopic update rules differ, the macroscopic, slow-time-scale physics—such as the fluctuation-dissipation relations—are identical for both methods. This confirms that the choice of simulation algorithm affects only the speed of convergence, not the final physical state reached.
main_problem: The paper compares the dynamical mean-field theory description of two Monte Carlo Markov Chain dynamics—synchronous (SyncMC) and asynchronous (Metropolis-Hastings, MH)—for mean-field spin glasses.
main_result: While the specific update rules and noise terms differ, both dynamics yield the same equations for slow time scales, including the fluctuation-dissipation ratio and the Parisi equation.
method: The authors use the Guionnet-Maïda formula and derive effective single-spin processes via Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) for both update schemes.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and the two dynamics (SyncMC vs. MH). It then derives the effective single-spin processes using DMFT, comparing the resulting equations and identifying the shared and unique terms for each dynamics. Finally, it confirms the equivalence of slow-time-scale physics via simulations.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous theoretical comparison of different simulation algorithms for complex, non-equilibrium systems, which is crucial for accurately modeling dynamics in disordered quantum or classical systems.
